en: Where are those who before us
May they always be in flower!
notes: lines 1.3 and 5.3: ':,:' is the original's repeat sign (the line is sung twice) and is kept as it stands.

lines 2.3-2.5: the sense is disputed. As written, 'Vadite' and 'Transite' are imperatives ('Go ... cross over'): to find the dead you must go to the heavens or the underworld, where they already are. Other versions read 'Abiere ad superos, transiere ad inferos' ('they have gone up ... gone down'), which this text does not have.
line 2.5: 'Ubi jam fuere' is literally 'where they already were', i.e. where they have long since been.
lines 4.3-4.4: 'membrum' is a member of the university (student or teacher), not a part of the body.
line 5.2: 'faciles' means easy, approachable, good-natured; it can also carry the sense 'compliant'.
line 6.4: 'Mecaenatum' (Maecenatum): of patrons, after Maecenas, Augustus's patron of poets; 'caritas' here is goodwill or generosity.
line 7.4: 'Antiburschius' is a student-Latin coinage: an enemy of the Burschen, the German students and their fraternities.
